findings_for_followup: The OIDC token is written to web-identity-token in the build workspace, .dockerignore does not exclude it and the Dockerfile runs COPY ., so it is very likely baked into the production image (inferred from three files, image not inspected)
Production deploys on push to main with only the :latest tag, no tests, scans or manual gate, and no rollback mechanism evidenced
Chromium snapshot 1135561 (about Chrome 114) and chromedriver 114.0.5735.90 are downloaded with no checksum from legacy hosts and run with --no-sandbox and a remote debugging port

The bot auto-sets manufacturer_accounts.isActive=false and schedule=false on matched login-error text; that flag gates sends from rest-api-evoke and patient-billing-schedule, so a false positive stops an account platform-wide
Most crawl failures are swallowed, so SQS never retries them; the restart-and-retry in main.py effectively covers Medtronic only; invalid events are dropped with only a Slack alert

main.py prints the whole incoming event, disconnected-monitor JSON and screenshots go to S3, noshow_disconnected_logs stores the whole event plus the public IP from api.ipify.org (called without a timeout per account); Slack carries usernames for halted accounts and some patient names
With includeAllAccounts the account name is overwritten with None, so S3 bodies and noshow_disconnected_logs rows carry account null and rows replace each other
Grouped crawl loop uses a stale loop variable for the manufacturer (TEST_REPORT with mixed manufacturers can crawl the wrong portal)
Account and manufacturer lists are hard-coded, so adding an account or manufacturer needs a deploy; a manufacturer missing from activeAccounts raises KeyError
sonar-project.properties carries the project key of manufacturer-hl7-parser and no pipeline step runs a scan; README says python main.py but main.py has no __main__ block
